source.title: Transition of AI Models in dependence of noise

record.tranche_reason: The study reports scaling results for image-classification accuracy under added noise, not held-out language-model cross-entropy, language-model scaling, or downstream language tasks. Its discussion and citation of language-model scaling do not test the claim.
record.gate_note: The study measures image-classification accuracy as image noise increases and the width of that transition against model size. These are related scaling results, but they do not measure the behavior named by any claim version. The paper cites Kaplan et al.; that citation is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures how image-classification accuracy under added Gaussian noise varies with model size: a shared critical noise and a power law in transition width. It does not measure held-out loss scaling with parameters, data or compute, compute-optimal allocation, shape effects, or downstream predictability. Transition width under noise is a related but different construct from V5's loss power law. Kaplan et al. is cited only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim more broadly that statistical-mechanics principles hold for AI. They describe a power law in accuracy decrease near the critical noise for the EfficientNet family. They hypothesise universality within a model class but say they cannot yet verify it. They propose extrapolating from small models to estimate model size for a given noise level.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Gaussian-noise corruption of image data and finite-size scaling of classification-accuracy transition widths, rather than language-model pretraining-loss sweeps over parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The transition-width fit is examined at different accuracy-level pairs; the authors report similar behavior across the selected levels.

fits_no_version.finding: EfficientNet B0–B7 (ImageNet21k-pretrained, evaluated on noisy Imagenette) share one critical noise for the accuracy collapse. The value is given as t ≈ 2000 in the text and 1845.934 in the Fig. 2 inset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The noise level at which classification accuracy collapses is independent of model size within a model family.

fits_no_version.finding: For EfficientNet-type CIFAR100 models over about three decades of parameter count, noise-transition width follows a power law with slope 0.27 ≃ 0.3, similar across accuracy-level pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The width of the noise-induced accuracy transition scales as a power law in parameter count (finite-size scaling).

record.problems: The study itself notes that its model variety is too limited to establish universality. The B0–B7 sizes cover approximately one decade, while the wider CIFAR100 sweep is described without a stated upper endpoint. No uncertainty estimates are given for the scaling fit, and the critical-noise value differs between the text and the Fig. 2 inset.

untested.parts: All: no language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no fitted loss law is extrapolated to larger runs. Extrapolation is only proposed.
All: no comparison of shape at fixed parameter count.
Loss power law in image models: the study measures noise-transition width, not loss scaling.
All: no downstream task predictability from scale or loss.
All: no comparison of fitting or setup choices for loss exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses classification is confirmed. The study is a physics-style finite-size scaling analysis of robustness to noise in image classifiers, not a test of neural scaling laws of loss. It has no uncertainty estimates, the width definition is ambiguous, and the critical-noise value is inconsistent between text and figure.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with language-model parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from fits to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal allocation of language-model parameters and training tokens as compute changes.
Effect of architecture details on language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
The study uses image classifiers, but does not test whether the same held-out-loss power law holds in image models or other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream language-task performance from language-model scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: EfficientNet B0–B7 (aggregate statement)
rows.size_stated: 5.3, 7.8, 9.2, 12, 19, 30, 43, and 66 (#Parameters; unit not stated in Table I)
rows.stage_stated: Pretrained on ImageNet21k and fine-tuned on ImageNet2012
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated classification accuracy on images with added noise

conditions.value: Corrupted Imagenette validation set, a subset of ImageNet2012

rows.value: The text reports a common critical noise of t ≈ 2000 and log(σc) ≈ 11; the Fig. 2 inset gives tc = 1845.934 for all models
rows.locator: Section IV, Fig. 2 and accompanying text
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the B0–B7 family. The text and figure inset give different numerical values for the critical point. This is image accuracy under corruption, not language-model loss.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. The critical noise is given as t ≈ 2000 in the text but tc = 1845.934 in the Fig. 2 inset. Sizes span about one decade, which the authors call inadequate for scaling.

rows.subject: EfficientNet-type models trained on CIFAR100 (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: The study says the sweep spans three decades and starts with 10000 parameters; upper endpoint not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured the noise-transition width at selected accuracy levels across model sizes

conditions.value: CIFAR100, evaluated on corrupted validation data
Accuracy-level pairs equally distant from 0.5, including (0.1, 0.9) and (0.2, 0.8)

rows.measure: Transition width Δacc versus parameter count
rows.locator: Section IV, Figs. 3–4 and accompanying text
rows.note: The authors say the different level sets behave similarly. The fitted power law concerns image-classification transition width under noise, not held-out pretraining loss.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. The width is defined inconsistently: once as |β(a_up) − β(a_low)|, then as Δacc = |a_up − a_low|. The fit has no uncertainty, and the sweep's upper endpoint is not stated.
